text.p: Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) has completed work on interconnection facilities in Monterrey for long-distance competitors due to enter the market in 1997, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
Telmex said the work was part of $505 million the company had invested in interconnection facilities.

The work included seven sites for jointly locating equipment belonging to Telmex and competitors, 31 fibre-optic and digital radio links, as well as 74 gateways to telephone exchanges, the company said.

Telmex, a state-owned company until 1991, loses its monopoly of long-distance telephone calls on January 1, 1997, in the city of Queretaro, and will have to face competition from January 10 in the northern industrial city of Monterrey.
Other cities will gradually come on line for competition.
